glofas.hard_boundary: GloFAS model layers are not local official warnings.

inventory_findings: The standard core already has a dedicated Germany flood-warning public capability backed only by NINA/LHP.
The general official weather-warning aggregate independently carries multiple flood and heavy-rain hazard types through DWD and NOAA/NWS.
The public flood-warning contract declares GLOF and ice-jam flood, but the current NINA title classifier has no direct GLOF or ice-jam patterns.
Heavy rain is a weather hazard type in weather.warning.official but is not part of natural_hazards.flood.warning.
GloFAS consists of nine separate raster contracts and must not be collapsed into an official-warning contract.
Flood reporting points, exceedance probabilities, forecast summaries, rapid mapping, rapid impact, and 100-year hazard climatology are materially different products.
Storm surge and coastal event are hydrology-adjacent but remain distinct from the P4-FLOOD river/pluvial/flash-flood subtype set.
open_questions_for_p4_flood_20: Define authoritative event semantics for river/general flood versus flash flood and surface-water/pluvial flood.
Decide whether heavy rain belongs only as a precursor/weather-warning class or can participate in a flood-specific additive semantic class.
Define how levee failure, dam failure, debris flow, GLOF and ice-jam flood remain distinct when multiple terms occur in one warning.
Decide whether the NINA title-only classifier is sufficient or whether additional source fields must be used.
Resolve declared-but-unreachable GLOF and ice-jam semantics in the dedicated NINA flood-warning path.
Keep official warning, modeled forecast/probability, rapid mapping/impact and climatology semantically separate.
Define whether weather.warning.official and natural_hazards.flood.warning are interchangeable, complementary, or distinct consumer intents.
Do not infer an official warning from a GloFAS threshold/probability or raster.
invariants: GloFAS model output is not an official warning.
Heavy rain is not automatically a flood event.
Flood probability is not an observed flood.
Rapid flood mapping is not automatically an authority-issued warning.
Storm surge and coastal event are not silently collapsed into river/pluvial flood.
Provider ID is not a scoring axis.
Endpoint reachability is not coverage proof.
